subject: general
question: As per India Justice Report 2025, how many judges does India have per million population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **India Justice Report 2025**, India has **15 judges per million population**, highlighting a significant shortage in judicial manpower.
 
• The report is a comprehensive analysis of the justice delivery system in India, covering areas like police, judiciary, prisons, and legal aid.
 
• This ratio demonstrates the challenges India faces in ensuring timely justice due to the limited number of judges compared to its large population.
 
• The **judge-to-population ratio** is an important metric used globally to assess the adequacy of judicial resources available to citizens.
 
• Efforts to increase the number of judges are ongoing, but the gap remains wide, impacting the efficiency of the Indian judicial system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India Justice Report:**

 
 
• The **India Justice Report** is published by **Tata Trusts** in collaboration with various organizations like the **Centre for Social Justice** and **Common Cause**.
 
• It ranks states based on their performance in delivering justice through police, judiciary, prisons, and legal aid.
 
• The report uses quantitative indicators to assess the functioning and effectiveness of the justice system.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Manpower in India:**
 
 
• India has a longstanding issue of a shortage of judges, which leads to delays in case resolution and contributes to a large backlog of cases.
 
• Compared to developed countries like the **United States** (which has over **100 judges per million population**), India’s ratio is significantly lower.
 
• To address this, the Indian government has been working to increase judicial appointments and improve infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in the Indian Judicial System:**
 
 
• The judicial system faces challenges such as case backlog, limited infrastructure, and slow recruitment processes.
 
• Lack of digitalization and poor connectivity in rural areas further hinder judicial efficiency.
 
• Judicial reforms, including the use of technology and better resource allocation, are crucial to addressing these challenges.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **National Judicial Infrastructure Authority of India (NJIAI)** is proposed to enhance judicial infrastructure.
 
• Efforts like **e-Courts** aim to digitize records and streamline case management.
 
• Regular training programs and workshops are conducted for judicial officers to improve efficiency and knowledge.
